Although the golden comment mentions a controller file while the candidate mentions a migration, the specific variable name and code pattern (`'#{h}'` with `embeddable_hosts`) confirm they are pointing to the same underlying issue (likely a misnamed file in the golden comment description).

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration reads embed_category by joining site_settings.value to categories.name, which fails for renamed categories or non-default locales

The migration resolves the target category with `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`. This joins the site setting's value (a category NAME) to `categories.name`. If the category was renamed after the setting was configured, or if the setting holds a slug rather than a name, or if multiple categories share a name (possible in different parents), the join returns zero or multiple rows. `[0]['id']` on an empty result raises NoMethodError (nil['id']), aborting the migration. The fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` only triggers when `category_id == 0`, not when the query crashes. More robust: look up by name with `Category.where(name: value).first` semantics, or rescue and default. Also, the migration deletes the `embed_category` and `embeddable_hosts` settings at the end (line 31) — if the INSERT loop fails midway (e.g. SQL injection crash or constraint violation), the settings are NOT deleted (good), but partial embeddable_hosts rows may already be inserted, and re-running the migration will duplicate them (no uniqueness constraint). Consider wrapping in a transaction (migrations are transactional by default in Rails, but `execute` DDL/DML is fine) and adding a uniqueness guard.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue explicitly identifies the exact same bug described in the golden comment: that accessing `[0]['id']` on the query result when it returns zero rows will raise a NoMethodError (`nil['id']`) and crash the migration instead of triggering the fallback.

false_positives.candidate:
Mass-assignment of arbitrary params into EmbeddableHost attributes

`save_host` assigns `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` directly from params without strong-parameter filtering or an allowlist. Any additional keys an admin POSTs under `embeddable_host[...]` are ignored only by luck of this explicit assignment, but more importantly there is no validation that `category_id` refers to an existing category before save; combined with `belongs_to :category` (no `validates :category, presence: true` on the model), an admin can set a dangling `category_id`. The model only validates the `host` format. Consider validating the category's existence (or at least that it is present) and using explicit permitted params.

record_for_host does case-insensitive lookup but stores mixed-case hosts, allowing duplicate/conflicting entries

`record_for_host` matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but the column has no uniqueness constraint and the model has no uniqueness validation, so two rows `Example.com` and `example.com` can both exist (the migration even inserts raw setting values without normalization). `host_allowed?` then returns the first match, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try(:category_id)` from an arbitrary one of them, so the category chosen for imported topics is nondeterministic. Add `validates :host, uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }` and a unique index on `lower(host)` (or downcase in before_validation) so lookups are deterministic.

Host validation regex is too permissive (allows paths, ports, and long TLDs), enabling referer-spoofing edge cases

The format regex `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i` permits an optional port and an arbitrary trailing path (`(\/.*)?`). However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host`, ignoring port and path, so a stored host of `example.com:8080` or `example.com/evil` will authorize ANY referer whose host is `example.com` regardless of port/path. That silently widens the embed allowlist beyond what the admin configured (e.g. allowing `http://example.com:8080` or any path on that host). Either strip/normalize to host-only on save (the before_validation already strips scheme and path but not port) and reject ports, or make `record_for_host` compare scheme+host+port consistently. At minimum, the stored value should be normalized to a bare hostname and the regex should not accept `:` or `/`.

Removing the 'embeddable hosts not set' guard lets embed/comments leak when no hosts are configured

The old code raised `Discourse::InvalidAccess.new('embeddable hosts not set') if SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.blank?` before checking the referer. The new code only checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)`. `host_allowed?` returns `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` returns `false` when the referer is nil/unparseable — so with zero configured hosts every request is still denied. However, the behavior change is subtle and untested: previously a blank setting was an explicit early failure; now the security of the endpoint depends entirely on `record_for_host` correctly returning false for nil/blank referers (it does via `uri.present?` / `host.present?` checks, and `URI(nil)` raises and is rescued to nil). The spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb line 13-16 ('raises an error with a missing host') covers the no-host case, but there is no test for a nil referer with hosts configured in the 'by topic id' context — actually there is (line 35-38). The real gap: `ensure_embeddable` rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` already rescues internally and returns false, so the rescue is dead code; more importantly, if `request.referer` is nil, `URI(nil)` raises `TypeError` (not `InvalidURIError`) inside `record_for_host`... actually `URI(nil)` raises `ArgumentError`/`TypeError` depending on Ruby version — `URI(nil)` raises `TypeError: no implicit conversion of nil into String` in modern Ruby, which is NOT rescued by `rescue nil` modifier? The modifier `rescue nil` catches StandardError; TypeError is a StandardError, so it is caught. OK — but this fragility (relying on exception class coverage) should be replaced with an explicit `return false if host.blank?` guard in `record_for_host`/`host_allowed?`.

EmbeddingSerializer serializes an OpenStruct, but has_many :embeddable_hosts with embed: :ids expects an association that OpenStruct does not provide

`fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding = OpenStruct.new(id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host))`. `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`. ActiveModel::Serializers' `has_many` with `embed: :ids` calls `object.embeddable_hosts` (works on OpenStruct via method_missing) and then maps to ids — this likely works, but `embed: :ids` means the response only contains `embeddable_host_ids: [...]` and NOT the embedded host objects. The Ember route does `this.store.find('embedding')` and the template iterates `embedding.embeddable_hosts` expecting full host objects with `host.host` and `host.category`. With `embed: :ids`, the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` (store.js.es6) looks up `root['embeddable_hosts']` (plural collection) in the payload — which is absent because ids-only embedding produces `embeddable_host_ids`. The `_lookupSubType` for the `embeddable_host_ids` key (matching `/(.+)_id(s?)$/`) will try to find each id in `root['embeddable_hosts']`, which is undefined, so `hydrated` will be `[undefined, ...]` and `obj['embeddable_hosts'] = [undefined...]`. The admin UI will render broken/empty rows. The serializer should use `embed: :objects` (or embed the objects with their serializer) so the payload contains an `embeddable_hosts` array, matching what the Ember store and template expect.

save() sends only the 'host' property, dropping category_id from the buffered changes and never persisting category edits

`const props = this.get('buffered').getProperties('host');` fetches only the `host` key from the buffer, then `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` is set on the props object. But `categoryId` is a separate component property bound to the `category-chooser`, and it is only initialized in the `edit()` action (`this.set('categoryId', this.get('host.category.id'))`). For a NEW host (created via `addHost`), `edit()` is never called, so `categoryId` stays `null`; when saving, `props.category_id = null` is sent, and the server-side `save_host` then defaults it to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` (controller line 25). So a newly added host can never be assigned a non-default category through the UI — the category chooser selection is silently discarded on create. Additionally, `getProperties('host')` returns the buffered host string, and assigning `props.category_id` mutates that plain object correctly, but if the buffer contained more keys they'd be dropped. The fix: build props explicitly, e.g. `const props = { host: this.get('buffered.host'), category_id: this.get('categoryId') }`, and initialize `categoryId` for new records (or bind the chooser directly to `buffered.category_id`).

After save, category is set from a possibly-null categoryId, desyncing the model from the server response

After a successful save, the code does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. If `categoryId` is null (new host saved without choosing a category — see related finding), `findById(null)` returns undefined and the host's `category` is set to undefined even though the server defaulted `category_id` to the uncategorized category. The server response (serialized with `rest_serializer: true`) contains the authoritative `category_id`, but it is ignored. The component should rely on the save response / `host.reload()` or at least fall back to the server-provided `category_id` rather than the possibly-stale local `categoryId`.

saveChanges action calls update({}) with no attributes and has no UI trigger

`saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` — an empty attribute hash. The `embedding` model is an OpenStruct-backed singleton with only `id` and `embeddable_hosts`; there are no editable scalar attributes on the embedding itself (all settings like embed_truncate remain site settings). The template (embedding.hbs) has no button wired to `saveChanges`, so this action is dead code that would issue a pointless PUT /admin/customize/embedding with an empty payload if ever invoked. Either remove the action or wire it to actual embedding-level settings; as written it is misleading dead code.

basePath type normalization breaks existing admin models whose type key uses underscores

`basePath` now does `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. `String.replace` with a string pattern replaces only the FIRST occurrence, and more importantly the check is applied to the raw `type` passed from the store. For the existing admin model `site-customization`, the store type key is `site-customization` (already dashed) so it still matches. But for `plugin` it matches. The new `embeddable-host` type is dashed, so it matches. However, if any caller uses the underscored form `embeddable_host` (e.g. `store.createRecord('embeddable_host')` as done in admin-embedding.js.es6 line 10!), `type.replace('_', '-')` converts it to `embeddable-host` and it matches — OK. But `Ember.String.underscore(store.pluralize(type))` in `pathFor` will pluralize `embeddable_host` to `embeddable_hosts` and underscore to `embeddable_hosts`, producing `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — while the Rails route is `resources :embeddable_hosts` under the admin namespace, which by default maps to `/admin/embeddable_hosts` — that matches. The subtle break: `type.replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore; a type like `foo_bar_baz` becomes `foo-bar_baz` and won't match a dashed ADMIN_MODELS entry. This is fragile; use `type.replace(/_/g, '-')` or `Ember.String.dasherize(type)` for correctness.

_hydrateEmbedded maps plural _ids keys without guarding against non-array values, producing [undefined] entries

The new plural branch does `obj[k].map(...)` whenever the key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with the `s` group. If a serializer sends `category_ids: null` or a non-array (e.g. a single id, or an empty string), `.map` either throws (null) or iterates characters (string), corrupting the hydrated object. There is no `Ember.isArray(obj[k])` guard. The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` where `hydrated` is the result of `.map` — if `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for a missing id, the array contains `undefined` entries rather than being filtered. This affects the new `embeddable_host_ids` embedding path (see EmbeddingSerializer finding): when the payload contains `embeddable_host_ids` but no `embeddable_hosts` collection, `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for each id and the model ends up with `embeddable_hosts = [undefined, undefined, ...]`. Add an `Ember.isArray` check and filter out undefined lookups.

Serializer exposes only category_id, but the Ember component reads host.category (object) for display and editing

`EmbeddableHostSerializer` emits `id, host, category_id`. The Ember component `embeddable-host.js.es6` reads `this.get('host.category.id')` in `edit()` and the template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`. With only `category_id` serialized (and the embedding payload using `embed: :ids` per the EmbeddingSerializer), the store's `_hydrateEmbedded` will attempt to resolve `category_id` via `_lookupSubType('category', ...)`, which special-cases categories via `Discourse.Category.findById(id)` — this works only if the category is already loaded client-side. For an admin page where categories may not be preloaded, `host.category` will be undefined and the badge renders blank, and `edit()` sets `categoryId` to undefined. The serializer should include the category object (e.g. `has_one :category` or a `category` attribute with BasicCategorySerializer) when `rest_serializer` is used for the embedding payload, or the component should use `host.category_id` directly with the category-chooser.

Authorization relies on redundant before_filter in addition to Admin::AdminController and route constraint

`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` inherits from `Admin::AdminController` (which already enforces staff access) and the route is declared with `constraints: AdminConstraint.new` (admin-only, routes.rb line 153). The explicit `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff` on line 3 is redundant — it downgrades the effective protection from admin-only (route constraint) to staff-only (moderators) at the controller layer. A moderator hitting the controller directly (if the route constraint were ever relaxed or bypassed) would pass `ensure_staff` but should not manage embeddable hosts. Other admin controllers in this codebase (e.g. permalinks, emojis) rely on the AdminConstraint route constraint and Admin::AdminController without re-declaring ensure_staff. Remove the redundant filter or change it to `ensure_admin` for defense in depth consistent with the AdminConstraint.

TopicEmbed.import silently creates topics in the uncategorized category when no EmbeddableHost matches the URL

`TopicEmbed.import` now does `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passes `category: eh.try(:category_id)` to PostCreator. `record_for_host` returns `false` (not nil) when the URL is unparseable or has no host, and returns `nil` when no DB row matches. `eh.try(:category_id)` on `false` returns nil (false doesn't respond to category_id, try returns nil), and on nil returns nil. So for any embed URL whose host is not in the allowlist, `category` is nil and PostCreator falls back to the default/uncategorized category. Previously the category came from the `embed_category` site setting, which was a single global default. Now, if an admin has not configured an EmbeddableHost for a feed URL, imported topics silently land in uncategorized instead of the configured embed category — a behavior regression for existing sites upgrading (the migration only creates EmbeddableHost rows from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting, and deletes `embed_category`; sites that relied on `embed_category` without listing every feed host in `embeddable_hosts` lose their category assignment). The import path should either reject URLs without a matching EmbeddableHost (since TopicRetriever already gates on `host_allowed?`) or fall back to a sensible default explicitly.

expandable_first_post? no longer checks that any embeddable host exists, changing behavior for sites with no hosts configured

`expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. The `embeddable_hosts.present?` guard was removed because the setting no longer exists. But the semantic of that guard was: only offer the 'expand embed' UI when embedding is actually enabled on the site (at least one allowed host). Now, on a site with zero EmbeddableHost rows, any topic that has a TopicEmbed (e.g. created via feed polling before hosts were removed, or imported by other means) will show the expandable first-post UI even though no external site is allowed to embed it. The correct replacement guard is `EmbeddableHost.exists?` (or checking that the topic's embed_url host is allowed). The spec was updated to fabricate an embeddable_host in the 'with an embeddable host' context, confirming the intent, but the production code lost the check entirely.

Controller spec only checks inheritance; no tests for create/update/destroy behavior or authorization

The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is a single assertion that the class is a subclass of Admin::AdminController. There are no tests for: creating a host (happy path + validation failure), updating a host, destroying a host, the nil-record 500 bug (see controller finding), authorization (non-staff/non-admin rejected), or the category_id defaulting to uncategorized when blank. Given this controller performs writes against a security-sensitive allowlist (embeddable hosts control which external sites can iframe the forum), the absence of any behavioral or authorization test is a significant gap. At minimum, add tests mirroring other admin controller specs: admin can create/update/destroy, moderator is denied (route constraint is AdminConstraint), invalid host returns 422, missing id returns 404 (once fixed).

Embedding controller spec only checks inheritance; show/update serialization untested

Like the embeddable_hosts spec, this spec contains only `expect(Admin::EmbeddingController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. The `show` action's serialization (EmbeddingSerializer with the OpenStruct, embed: :ids behavior) and the `update` action are completely untested. Given the serializer/store contract concerns around `embed: :ids` vs the Ember client expecting embedded objects (see EmbeddingSerializer finding), a serialization spec asserting the JSON shape of GET /admin/customize/embedding is essential. Add a test that GETs the show action as admin and asserts the response contains the expected structure (embeddable_hosts with id/host/category_id), and that non-admins are rejected.

update action is a no-op that re-renders show; PUT /admin/customize/embedding accepts and ignores any payload

`update` simply re-renders the embedding serializer without reading or applying any params. The route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` (routes.rb line 139) accepts a PUT with an arbitrary body and returns 200 with the current embedding state, silently discarding whatever the client sent. The Ember adapter's `update` (rest.js.es6 line 56) sends `data[typeField] = attrs` and expects `json[typeField]` back. This is a misleading API: clients may believe settings were saved. Either implement actual update semantics (e.g. accept embed_truncate and other embedding settings) or remove the PUT route and the `saveChanges` controller action to avoid a dead, misleading endpoint.

resources :embeddable_hosts generates an index/show route that has no controller action

`resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates all RESTful routes including GET /admin/embeddable_hosts (index) and GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id (show). `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy` — there are no `index` or `show` actions. A request to those routes will raise AbstractController::ActionNotFound (or UnknownFormat) → 500/404. Since the Ember client fetches hosts via the embedding endpoint (GET /admin/customize/embedding), the index/show routes are unnecessary. Restrict the resource: `resources :embeddable_hosts, only: [:create, :update, :destroy], constraints: AdminConstraint.new`.

Template hides the entire hosts table (and shows nothing) when there are zero hosts, with no empty-state message

`{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the whole table. When no hosts exist, the admin sees only the 'Add Host' button with no explanation, and — combined with the EmbeddingSerializer `embed: :ids` issue — `embedding.embeddable_hosts` may be undefined or an array of undefined entries even when hosts exist, causing the table to render with broken rows or not at all. Add an `{{else}}` branch with an empty-state message (e.g. i18n 'admin.embedding.no_hosts'), and ensure the serializer actually embeds host objects so the `if` evaluates correctly.

@on('didInsertElement') combined with @observes('editing') refocuses the input on every edit toggle, fighting user interaction

The `_focusOnInput` method is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The observer fires whenever `editing` changes (i.e., when entering AND leaving edit mode). When leaving edit mode (editing becomes false), the observer still schedules `this.$('.host-name').focus()` in afterRender — but by then the input may no longer exist (the `{{#if editing}}` block has been torn down), so `this.$('.host-name')` is an empty jQuery set and `.focus()` is a no-op; harmless but sloppy. More importantly, the observer firing on `editing` becoming false is unintended. The intent is clearly to focus only when entering edit mode. Use `@observes('editing')` with a guard `if (this.get('editing'))`, or better, drop the observer and call the focus logic explicitly from the `edit()` action and `didInsertElement` when `host.isNew`.

destroyRecord failure leaves the host in the list and gives no feedback beyond the generic ajax error popup

In the `delete` action, `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); })` only removes the host from the controller's list on success. There is no `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save`), so if the DELETE request fails (e.g. the nil-record 500 from the controller, or a network error), the promise rejection is unhandled — no error is shown to the admin and the row stays. The user gets no feedback that deletion failed. Add `.catch(popupAjaxError)` to match the `save` action's error handling.

No test for blank/nil host (the before_validation nil crash) and no uniqueness validation test

The spec tests trimming of http/https/paths and host_allowed? matching, but does not test: (1) `EmbeddableHost.new(host: nil).valid?` or `EmbeddableHost.new(host: '').valid?` — which currently crashes with NoMethodError in before_validation (see model finding); (2) duplicate host rejection (case-insensitive) — the model has no uniqueness validation; (3) that `record_for_host` returns false for nil/blank/unparseable input (the security-critical path used by EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever). Adding these tests would pin down the nil-crash bug and the case-insensitive duplicate issue.

count action renders JSONP with unvalidated callback parameter (pre-existing, but now more exposed without host gate context)

`render json: {counts: by_url}, callback: params[:callback]` reflects the `callback` query parameter directly into a JSONP response. While this is pre-existing code and not changed by this PR, the PR removes the `embeddable_hosts` blank-check from `ensure_embeddable` (which also gates `count`), meaning the JSONP reflection is now reachable in configurations where previously a blank setting would have blocked it. A malicious `callback` value could be used for reflected content injection in browsers that render the response as HTML (JSONP callback injection). This should be validated against a whitelist regex (e.g. `/\A[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*\z/`) or removed in favor of CORS. Flagging because the PR's change to `ensure_embeddable` alters the exposure of this endpoint.

category-chooser bound to categoryId which is not initialized for new records, so new hosts cannot pick a category

The `{{category-chooser value=categoryId}}` binds to the component's `categoryId` property, which is initialized to `null` (component line 9) and only set in the `edit()` action. For a new host row (created via `addHost` → `store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`), `edit()` is never invoked (the row starts in editing mode because `host.isNew` is true), so `categoryId` remains null. The chooser shows no selection, and on save `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` sends null, which the server replaces with the uncategorized category. The admin's category selection for a new host is therefore always ignored. Initialize `categoryId` when the host is new (e.g. in `didInsertElement` if `host.isNew`, set it to the default/uncategorized category id) or bind the chooser to `buffered.category_id` so it participates in the buffer lifecycle.

Plural _ids hydration assigns undefined entries instead of filtering missing lookups

In the new plural branch of `_hydrateEmbedded`, `obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); })` — when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined (id not found in the root collection), the resulting array contains `undefined` holes. The subsequent `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` keeps those holes. Downstream code iterating `embeddable_hosts` (e.g. the `{{#each}}` in embedding.hbs) will render rows for `undefined` entries, causing template errors (`Cannot read property 'host' of undefined`). The single-id branch guards with `if (hydrated)`, but the plural branch has no equivalent filter. Add `.filter(function(h) { return !!h; })` or use `Ember.A()` with compact semantics.

Locale string 'Allowed Hosts' is used as a table column header for a single host value

The locale key `admin.embedding.host: "Allowed Hosts"` (plural) is used in embedding.hbs line 4 as the column header for the host column (`{{i18n "admin.embedding.host"}}`). A column listing individual hostnames should be singular ("Host" or "Allowed Host"), not plural "Allowed Hosts". The plural reads incorrectly as a section title. Change to `host: "Host"` (or "Allowed Host") for the column header.

Silent fallback to uncategorized_category_id when category_id is blank may hide admin configuration errors

`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` silently substitutes the uncategorized category whenever the client sends a blank/nil category_id. Combined with the Ember component bug (categoryId not initialized for new hosts), this means a new host created without explicitly choosing a category is silently assigned to uncategorized — the admin may believe they set a category that was never sent. While the fallback prevents a NOT NULL violation (category_id is null: false in the migration), it masks client/server contract mismatches. Consider returning a validation error when category_id is blank on create (forcing the UI to send a valid category), or at minimum ensure the UI always sends a valid category_id (see component finding).

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Wrong lightness value in dark-theme branch of embedded-post username link

In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the change replaced `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, which is a much lighter color than the original. This alters the appearance of the light theme (username links in embedded/reply-to posts become significantly lighter), not just the dark theme. The light-theme value should have been preserved at 30% (i.e. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same CSS selector, the exact same code change, and the exact same problem (the lightness value for the light theme in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was inadvertently changed from 30% to 70%).

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Wrong lightness value in .group-member-info .name dark-light-choose

In `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info .name`, the change replaced `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. More importantly, the database has a UNIQUE index on users.email (index_users_on_email UNIQUE per the schema comment), which in PostgreSQL is case-sensitive, so 'Foo@bar.com' and 'foo@bar.com' can both be inserted, creating two accounts that downstream code (which downcases before lookup) will treat as the same person — enabling account impersonation/confusion in email-based lookups, password resets, and the DiscourseHub nickname matching. `. In the main Discourse UI, cooked post HTML is produced by the Markdown pipeline which sanitizes dangerous markup; here `raw` bypasses any escaping. For posts created through TopicEmbed this cooked content is entirely unsanitized external HTML (see the TopicEmbed raw_html finding), so any script in an imported article executes in the context of the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe. Even for normal cooked posts, re-rendering with `raw` in a separate layout that lacks the standard CSP/onebox protections weakens the XSS posture. The embed view should render cooked content through the same sanitization used elsewhere, and imported raw_html posts must never reach this template unsanitized.

import mutates the caller's contents string via <<

Line 13 does `contents << "\n<hr>..."`, which mutates the String object passed in by the caller. In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35 the content is `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` — a fresh string, so it's mostly harmless there, but in app/models/topic_embed.rb import_remote line 52, `doc.content` (the Readability result) is passed and then mutated; any caller reusing the string (e.g. computing the sha1 before/after, or the Disqus importer in lib/tasks/disqus.thor) will see the appended footer. Note also that `content_sha1` on line 16 is computed AFTER the mutation, so the stored hash includes the footer — meaning an update comparison is consistent, but the mutation of a caller-owned object is a hidden side effect that can corrupt data if the same string is reused (e.g. the spec at spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb line 40 calls import twice with different literals, masking the issue). Use `contents = contents + ...` or `<<` on a dup.

Check-then-act race in TopicEmbed.import allows duplicate topics for the same URL

import does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if blank, creates a topic/post/TopicEmbed inside a transaction. There is a unique index on embed_url (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb line 11), but the existence check happens before the transaction and outside any locking, so two concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g. PollFeed running hourly while a user hits /embed/best and enqueues RetrieveTopic, or two Sidekiq workers) can both see `embed.blank?`, both create topics, and the second `TopicEmbed.create!` will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique — leaving an orphaned topic+post created by PostCreator (the transaction wraps it, so it rolls back, but the failure is unhandled and the job has retry: false in poll_feed.rb line 12, so the item is silently lost). The correct pattern is to attempt the create and rescue RecordNotUnique, or lock/upsert. At minimum the job should handle the race gracefully.

CGI.unescapeHTML on feed content corrupts HTML entities and double-unescapes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` unescapes HTML entities in the feed content before it is stored as raw_html. RSS content is already HTML (often entity-encoded, e.g. `<p>` for a literal `

` in a code sample, or `&` for a literal `&`). Unescaping turns `<script>` into a real `

feed_key is defined but never used — Last-Modified/ETag caching is dead code

The job defines `feed_key` (a Redis key `feed-modified:<sha1 of url>`) but nothing in the file ever reads or writes it. The apparent intent was to send If-Modified-Since / track the feed's Last-Modified header and skip re-parsing unchanged feeds, but `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` every hour and re-imports every item (TopicEmbed.import does dedupe by content_sha1, so it's not catastrophic, but every item's content is re-hashed and compared each hour, and the HTTP fetch always happens). Either implement the conditional GET using feed_key or remove the dead method; as written it misleads maintainers into thinking conditional requests are happening.

invalid_host? returns true when embeddable_host is blank, but comparison is exact-host and case-sensitive

`SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host` compares the configured host string directly to the URI host. If embeddable_host is configured as `http://eviltrout.com` (with scheme) or `Eviltrout.com` (mixed case) or `eviltrout.com/` (trailing slash), the comparison fails for perfectly valid embed URLs and retrieval is silently skipped; conversely `www.eviltrout.com` vs `eviltrout.com` mismatches. The setting is documented as "Host that can embed the comments" (config/locales/server.en.yml), so it should be normalized (strip scheme, downcase, strip port) before comparison, and the embed_url host should be compared as a suffix of the configured registrable domain. As written, misconfiguration silently disables the entire feature.

Calling Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside RetrieveTopic defeats the purpose of the async job and can recurse

perform_retrieve runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when feed polling is enabled. RetrieveTopic is itself a Sidekiq job enqueued from the embed controller; running the entire hourly feed poll synchronously inside it means a single embed request can trigger a full feed fetch and import of every item, blocking the RetrieveTopic worker for a long time (PollFeed does unbounded HTTP fetches with no timeout). Worse, PollFeed imports items via TopicEmbed.import, which is fine, but if any code path enqueues RetrieveTopic from within PollFeed processing there is potential for long chains; more practically, the design intent (per the class comment "First check RSS if that is enabled") is to check whether the feed already contains the URL, not to run the whole poll. This should instead query the feed (or a cached copy) for the specific embed_url, or enqueue PollFeed asynchronously and return, letting the loading page's 30-second reload pick up the result.

fetch_http performs an unvalidated server-side request to a user-influenced URL (SSRF surface)

fetch_http calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)`, which does `open(url).read` (app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48). The URL originates from the `embed_url` query parameter of the public `/embed/best` endpoint (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 9). The only validation is `invalid_host?`, which checks `URI(@embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. This still allows SSRF-style abuse within the allowed host (e.g. `http://eviltrout.com:22/`, `http://eviltrout.com/admin/internal-endpoint`, `http://user:pass@eviltrout.com/`, or `file://` if the host string is ever misconfigured to match), and `open()` follows redirects by default, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` (cloud metadata) or an internal service will be fetched and its content imported as a post. open-uri must be restricted: validate scheme is http/https, resolve and reject private/loopback/link-local IPs, disable redirects or re-validate each hop, and set timeouts.

import_remote fetches arbitrary URLs with open() — no scheme, redirect, or private-network restrictions

`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` uses Kernel#open (open-uri) on a URL that, via TopicRetriever/RetrieveTopic, is ultimately derived from the public embed_url parameter, and via PollFeed from feed item links/ids (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` in poll_feed.rb line 33 — note this fallback accepts ANY string as a URL, including `file:///etc/passwd`, which open-uri will happily open). There is no scheme whitelist, no redirect limit, no timeout, and no protection against requests to internal/private IP ranges. This is a full SSRF primitive: an attacker who can influence a feed item id/link (or an embed_url on the allowed host that redirects) can make the server read local files (`file://`) or internal HTTP services and import the response body as a forum post, leaking internal data. The fetch must be hardened (scheme whitelist, redirect re-validation, IP range blocking, timeouts).

Feed item id used as URL without any validation enables file:// and internal URL fetch

`url = i.link; url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`. When an RSS item has no link (or a non-http link), the item's `id` (often a GUID, which in many feeds is a URN like `urn:uuid:...`, a tag URI, or — in attacker-controlled feeds — an arbitrary string such as `file:///etc/passwd` or `http://169.254.169.254/`) is used as the URL and passed to TopicEmbed.import → import_remote → `open(url)`. TopicEmbed.import line 11 does check `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and returns nil otherwise, which blocks file:// at that layer — but only for the import path; the regex is also loose (matches `https://` anywhere at the start, accepts `https://` followed by anything). The deeper issue is that poll_feed hands unvalidated feed data to a URL fetcher; the id fallback should be removed or strictly validated, and the fetch layer must enforce scheme/IP restrictions regardless (defense in depth).

RetrieveTopic job is enqueued on every cache miss with no deduplication, enabling job flooding

When no TopicEmbed exists for the embed_url, the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders the loading page, which auto-reloads every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb line 10). Each reload re-enters `best`, finds no embed (the job may still be running or throttled), and enqueues another RetrieveTopic job. TopicRetriever has a 60-second Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?`), but that only prevents the actual fetch — the jobs still pile up in Sidekiq, and each one performs DB queries and, for staff users (`no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)`), bypasses the throttle entirely. A popular embed (or a bot hitting /embed/best?embed_url=... directly with a valid Referer) can enqueue thousands of jobs. The controller should check the throttle key (or use a single enqueue-per-URL lock) before enqueueing, and the loading page should back off.

TopicView is built with current_user, leaking private topic data into the public embed

`TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` passes the current user. The embed endpoint is meant to be loaded in an iframe on a third-party site; the iframe request will typically carry the Discourse session cookie of whatever user happens to view the host page (cookies are sent on iframe requests depending on SameSite settings). If that user is a staff member or a member of a restricted category, TopicView will include posts/topics they can see but anonymous visitors cannot, and the rendered HTML (including post content from restricted categories) is served to the third-party page. The embed view must always be built as an anonymous/system user (e.g. `TopicView.new(topic_id, nil, ...)` or a dedicated embed user) and should verify the topic is publicly visible before rendering. As written, restricted/private post content can be exfiltrated by embedding a URL.

Update path revises the post but never updates the topic title

When content changes, import revises the post via PostRevisor with the new contents, but the topic title (from the feed item's `i.title`) is never updated — only the initial creation uses `title`. A feed that renames an article leaves the Discourse topic with the stale original title forever. Additionally, `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` skips validations/callbacks (acceptable here) but if the PostRevisor revision fails silently (revise! returns false when raw is unchanged — though sha1 differs so raw differs — or raises), the sha1 is still updated only after revise! returns, which is correct, but there is no transaction wrapping the revise + update_column, so a crash between them leaves the post updated but the sha1 stale, causing a redundant re-revision next poll (harmless but noisy). The title update is the real gap: PollFeed passes `i.title` on every run but import ignores it on the update path.

absolutize_urls only handles root-relative URLs and mishandles protocol-relative and default ports

absolutize_urls rewrites only hrefs/srcs that `start_with?('/')`. Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/x.jpg`) and scheme-relative paths (`http://other.com/...` is fine, but `//host/path` is left as-is and will resolve against the Discourse origin when rendered, breaking images/links). Also, the port logic `prefix << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443` appends the port for https URLs on port 80 or http URLs on port 443 incorrectly (e.g. `https://host:80/` would get `:80` appended even though URI normalizes... actually URI keeps explicit ports, so `https://eviltrout.com:80/` yields prefix `https://eviltrout.com:80` which is wrong-ish but functional). More importantly, relative URLs like `images/foo.jpg` (no leading slash) are not absolutized at all and will 404 when rendered from the Discourse origin. The method should use URI.join semantics for all relative references, not just root-relative ones.

Avatar img src uses ERB interpolation inside a single-quoted HTML attribute without escaping `` interpolates the avatar URL into a single-quoted attribute with no HTML escaping. small_avatar_url is derived from the user's uploaded avatar or gravatar; an admin/user-controlled avatar URL containing a single quote would break out of the attribute. Rails' `image_tag` (used correctly on lines 8 and 26) escapes properly; this raw img tag should use `image_tag(post.user.small_avatar_url)` or at least `h()` the value. Low severity because avatar URLs are largely system-generated, but it's an inconsistency with the rest of the file and a latent injection point if avatar URLs ever become user-supplied strings.

Controller spec expects TopicRetriever to be used, but the controller enqueues a job instead

The test "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" stubs `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, but the controller (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb line 15) never calls TopicRetriever directly — it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The spec would fail against the actual implementation (TopicRetriever.new is never invoked in the controller), meaning either the spec is wrong or the controller was changed after the spec was written and the test suite is red. A correct test would expect `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (or `Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, ...)`). This is exactly the kind of spec that gives false confidence — it documents an implementation that doesn't exist.

Update-path spec doesn't verify the content_sha1 changed or that a revision was created

The "Supports updating the post" test only asserts `post.cooked.should =~ /new contents/`. It doesn't verify that the TopicEmbed's content_sha1 was updated (so the next poll with the same content won't re-revise), that a PostRevision was created, or that the returned post is the same post (same id) as the original. A regression where import creates a second topic on update (the race condition described in the concurrency finding) would still pass this test as long as cooked contains the new text. The test should assert `post.id == original_post.id`, `TopicEmbed.count == 1`, and the updated sha1.

discourse_expires_in 1.minute is applied even to the loading page, causing rapid re-fetch churn

`discourse_expires_in 1.minute` sets a 1-minute HTTP cache on both the rendered topic view and the loading page. For the loading page this is mostly harmless, but combined with the 30-second auto-reload in loading.html.erb, a shared/CDN cache could serve a stale loading page for up to a minute after the topic has actually been imported, making the embed appear stuck. More importantly, caching the rendered best view for only 1 minute means every embed impression after the first minute hits the Rails stack and rebuilds a TopicView (an expensive operation) — for a high-traffic embed this is a significant load multiplier. The cache duration should be longer for the success path (the content changes only when the topic changes) and the loading page should send no-cache headers so the reload actually re-queries.

no_throttle is granted based on the user_id passed from the controller, which is the iframe viewer's identity

`TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))` — the user_id comes from `current_user.try(:id)` in the embed controller, i.e. whichever Discourse user's browser loaded the third-party page. Any staff member who visits a page containing an embed (or an attacker who socially engineers a staff member to a page with many distinct embed_urls) gets the 60-second throttle disabled, allowing unbounded fetch/import of arbitrary URLs on the allowed host. The throttle bypass should not be tied to the viewer's identity at all; if staff bypass is desired it should be a server-side decision, and the throttle key should also incorporate the URL (it does) but the bypass should be removed or gated on a server-controlled flag.

cook_method default of 1 does not match Post.cook_methods enum ordering

The migration sets `default: 1, null: false` for posts.cook_method. Post.cook_methods is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` (app/models/post.rb lines 63-65). Discourse's Enum assigns values starting at 1 in declaration order (regular=1, raw_html=2) — so default 1 = regular, which is correct. However, this is fragile: the migration hardcodes the integer 1 instead of referencing the enum, and the schema comment in post.rb doesn't list cook_method at all (the annotate block at the bottom of post.rb is missing the new column). If the enum order ever changes, existing rows silently change meaning. The migration should use a comment documenting the mapping, and the model's schema annotation should be regenerated to include cook_method. More importantly, `Post#cook` (line 133) compares `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` — for legacy rows defaulted to 1 this is regular, fine, but there's no DB check constraint tying the value to the enum, so a bad value (0, 3) silently falls through to the regular cook path.

cook_method raw_html bypasses all cooking/sanitization with no guard on who can set it

`cook` returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The only setter is PostCreator line 216 (`post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method] if @opts[:cook_method].present?`), and PostCreator is a public API used by controllers with user-supplied opts in many places. Any code path that passes user-controlled opts through to PostCreator (e.g. a plugin, the API, or a future controller) can set cook_method to raw_html and store arbitrary unsanitized HTML. There is no Guardian check restricting raw_html to staff/import contexts. The raw_html path should be gated (e.g. only settable when the acting user is staff or via an explicit import flag checked against the guardian), and the value should be validated against the enum on assignment.

skip_validations option now skips post validations on revise, but the raw_html cook_method is never re-applied on revision

The diff changes `@post.save` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, which is needed for the import update path. However, when TopicEmbed.import revises a raw_html post (topic_embed.rb line 36), PostRevisor.update_post sets `@post.raw = @new_raw` and saves; the before_save callback in post.rb (line 321) recomputes `self.cooked = cook(raw, ...)` only `unless new_record?` — for an existing raw_html post, cook returns raw, so cooked is correctly set to the new raw. That part works. The subtle issue: `skip_validations` now bypasses Validators::PostValidator for ALL revisions when the option is passed, including length/entropy/spam checks — acceptable for the import path, but the option is a general-purpose footgun now available to any caller of PostRevisor. It should be named/scoped to the import use case or documented. Low severity since only TopicEmbed passes it today.

Loading page reloads unconditionally every 30s with no cap, hammering the server for never-imported URLs

The loading view does `setTimeout(function() { document.location.reload(); }, 30000)` with no maximum retry count and no backoff. If the URL can never be imported (host not actually embeddable, fetch fails, user not found — TopicRetriever.fetch_http returns silently if embed_by_username is blank), the iframe reloads forever, each time enqueueing another RetrieveTopic job (see the controller finding). A single abandoned embed tab generates 2 requests/minute indefinitely plus a Sidekiq job each time. The reload should stop after N attempts and show a permanent message with a link to start the discussion on the forum.

Embed route has no rate limiting and is unauthenticated

`get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` is a public, unauthenticated route with no rate limit. Combined with the job-enqueue-per-miss behavior and the TopicView construction on hit, it's an easy DoS/amplification vector: an attacker can request /embed/best?embed_url=<unique-string> with a spoofed Referer matching embeddable_host, each request enqueuing a Sidekiq job and (for existing topics) building a full TopicView. There is no RateLimiter usage in EmbedController. The endpoint should be rate limited per IP (and per embed_url), and the referer check should be supplemented with a per-IP limiter since the Referer is trivially spoofable.

URL validation regex is too loose and inconsistent with the rest of the codebase

`return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` accepts strings like `https://` (nothing after), `https://?x`, `https:// evil.com`, and `https://example.com/redirect?to=javascript:...`. It also uses escaped colons (`\:`) which are unnecessary in a regex. Elsewhere the codebase uses the same loose pattern (poll_feed.rb line 33), so the inconsistency is systemic, but the import path is the security boundary: a URL like `https://eviltrout.com@evil.com/` (userinfo trick) passes the regex and URI parsing will treat evil.com as the host — which then fails invalid_host? in TopicRetriever, but TopicEmbed.import is also called directly from PollFeed with feed-supplied URLs that bypass TopicRetriever's host check entirely. The URL should be parsed with URI() and validated: scheme in [http, https], host present, and host matching the expected domain.

PollFeed spec requires the wrong dependency and never tests poll_feed itself

The spec requires `jobs/regular/process_post` (line 2) — an unrelated job — instead of `jobs/scheduled/poll_feed`, and all four tests only exercise the `execute` guard conditions by mocking `poll_feed`. There is no test that poll_feed actually parses a feed, handles a missing user, handles a malformed feed, or calls TopicEmbed.import with the right arguments. The require of process_post suggests a copy-paste error and means the spec may not even load the class under test in some configurations. The spec should require the correct file and include tests for poll_feed's behavior (using a stubbed SimpleRSS.parse / fakeweb, both of which are available in the Gemfile).

Disqus import rewritten to TopicEmbed.import_remote but reply posts are created with raw HTML cooked content and no cook_method

The diff replaces the old PostCreator-based topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, then creates reply posts with `attrs = { ..., raw: p[:cooked], cooked: p[:cooked], ... }` (lines 160-165). The Disqus `message` field is HTML from the export; setting both raw and cooked to that HTML and creating via PostCreator means the post goes through the normal Markdown cook pipeline (cook_method defaults to regular), which will mangle the HTML (Markdown-processed HTML often renders incorrectly), and the before_save callback recomputes cooked from raw anyway. The replies should either be created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (matching the imported topic) or converted to Markdown. As written, imported Disqus replies will be double-processed and likely display broken markup. Also, `Date.parse(p[:created_at])` will raise on malformed dates, aborting the whole import with no error handling.

Disqus import creates users from unvalidated author emails with no approval

`post_user = User.create!(email: email, username: UserNameSuggester.suggest(email))` creates a full user account for every distinct author email in the Disqus export, with no validation of the email beyond `Email.downcase`, no check against the email blacklist (which is explicitly cleared on line 141: `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist = ""`), and no approval/trust gating. A malicious Disqus export (the import file is operator-supplied, but exports can be crafted) can create thousands of accounts with arbitrary email addresses, which then appear as post authors. These auto-created users have trust level 0 but can still be spam vectors (they exist, can be messaged, appear in user lists). The import should use a dedicated import user or staged/unapproved accounts, and the blacklist should not be globally disabled for the duration.

Referer host comparison doesn't handle missing port/scheme normalization and is case-sensitive

`URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` — URI#host returns a downcased host without port, but SiteSetting.embeddable_host is compared as a raw string. If the admin enters `Eviltrout.com` or `eviltrout.com:80` or `http://eviltrout.com` in the setting, the comparison fails for every request and the feature is entirely broken (all requests raise InvalidAccess). The setting should be normalized once (downcase, strip scheme/port) before comparison, or the comparison should parse the setting as a URI too. The spec (embed_controller_spec.rb) only tests with an exact lowercase match, so this misconfiguration is untested.

Script assumes #discourse-comments exists; throws if the host page lacks it

`document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` can return null if the host page doesn't include the expected div (typo, different embed snippet version, CSP-modified DOM), and `comments.appendChild(iframe)` on line 12 then throws a TypeError, breaking the entire script. The embed snippet should be documented as requiring the div, but the script should guard: `if (!comments) { return; }`. Low severity (host-page integration issue), but it silently breaks embedding with no error message.

import_remote fetches the full page with no timeout, size limit, or redirect limit

`Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` reads the entire response body into memory with open-uri defaults: no open_timeout/read_timeout, no redirect limit (open-uri follows up to 10 redirects by default), and no maximum size. A slow or huge page on the allowed host (or an allowed-host URL redirecting to a multi-GB file) will hang the Sidekiq worker and consume unbounded memory. The fetch should use explicit timeouts, a redirect cap with re-validation, and a maximum content length.

TopicRetriever spec never tests the actual retrieval, throttling, or host validation logic end-to-end

All tests mock `perform_retrieve` or `retrieved_recently?`, so the spec verifies only the wiring of `retrieve` (that it calls perform_retrieve unless invalid_host?/retrieved_recently?). It never tests that invalid_host? correctly parses URIs, that retrieved_recently? actually uses Redis setnx/expire correctly (the throttle could be broken and no test would catch it), that perform_retrieve checks TopicEmbed existence, or that fetch_http looks up the embed user. The Redis throttle in particular is concurrency-sensitive logic that deserves a real test (mock_redis is available in the Gemfile).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client-side file size validation hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring site settings for max image/attachment size

The change from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) removes the client-side validation against the actual configured site settings. If an admin sets `max_image_size_kb` to 1MB (1024 KB), the client will still allow uploads up to 10MB before the server rejects them or attempts to downsize them. This creates a poor user experience: users can select and upload files up to 10MB that will then be processed server-side (potentially downsized or rejected), wasting bandwidth and time. The client-side check should use the actual site setting value to provide immediate feedback. The same issue exists on line 246 for the 413 error handler.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue accurately identifies the exact same problem described in the golden comment: replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` causes client-side validation to ignore site settings, and it also explicitly notes the same issue in the 413 error handler below.

false_positives.candidate:
Downsize loop uses file size in bytes compared against kilobytes setting, causing incorrect comparison

The condition `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` compares the tempfile size (in bytes) against `max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (which converts KB to bytes). However, `tempfile.size` returns bytes, and `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` also returns bytes (e.g., 1024 * KB value). This comparison is actually correct for bytes vs bytes. BUT the real bug is on line 67: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes "80%" as the dimensions parameter. Looking at `downsize_instructions`, this becomes `-resize 80%\>` which is a percentage resize, not a size-based downsize. The loop condition checks if file size exceeds the limit, but the downsize operation only reduces dimensions by 20% each iteration (80% of current size). For a very large image (e.g., 50MB), 5 iterations of 80% reduction only gets to ~32% of original dimensions, which may still result in a file larger than the limit. More critically, if the image is already small in dimensions but large in file size (e.g., uncompressed PNG), resizing won't help reduce file size proportionally. The loop may exit with `attempt == 0` while the file is still over the size limit, and the upload proceeds anyway with an oversized file.

Downsize writes to same path as input, risking data corruption if ImageMagick fails

`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` passes the same path for both `from` and `to` parameters. The `downsize_instructions` generates a command like `convert /tmp/file.png[0] -gravity center -background transparent -resize 80%\> /tmp/file.png`. ImageMagick's `convert` command reads the input file completely before writing output, so this usually works, but if the process is interrupted, crashes, or runs out of disk space during the write, the original file is corrupted/truncated. The tempfile would then contain a partial or corrupt image, and `Upload.create_for` on line 72 would create an upload record for a corrupted file. This is a data integrity risk. The code should write to a separate temporary file and then replace the original only on success.

Downsize loop doesn't verify success of downsize operation before continuing

The while loop on lines 66-69 calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores the return value. `downsize` (via `convert_with`) returns `false` if the ImageMagick command fails or if `ImageOptim` optimization fails. If downsize fails (e.g., corrupt image, missing ImageMagick, unsupported format), the loop continues decrementing `attempt` and retrying 5 times on the same unchanged file, wasting CPU and time, then proceeds to create an upload with the original oversized file. The code should check the return value and break or handle the error appropriately.

API URL download limit increased from max_image_size_kb to 10MB, bypassing size restrictions

The change from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` increases the maximum download size for API-provided URLs from the configured `max_image_size_kb` (which could be e.g., 1MB or 2MB) to a hardcoded 10MB. This allows API clients to make the server download much larger files than the site's configured image size limit. While the subsequent downsize loop attempts to reduce the size, this still allows: (1) temporary disk usage of up to 10MB per request, (2) network bandwidth consumption downloading 10MB files, (3) potential DoS if many API requests are made with URLs pointing to large files. The original limit was tied to the site setting; the new hardcoded 10MB removes that protection. The download limit should remain tied to a configurable maximum, or at least be documented as a deliberate security tradeoff.

content_type is nil for API URL uploads, potentially causing incorrect MIME type detection

When uploading via API URL (line 54-56), `content_type` is never set (it's only set in the `else` branch on line 60). The downsize block on lines 64-70 runs before `Upload.create_for` on line 72, which receives `content_type: content_type` (nil for URL uploads). While this may have been the case before this PR, the new downsize logic specifically processes images, and having `content_type` nil means the upload record may not have the correct content type set. This could affect how the file is served later (Content-Type header) and whether it's treated as an image for thumbnail generation. The `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` check on line 64 uses the filename extension, but the actual content_type stored in the upload may be nil or incorrectly detected.

Error message for 413 uses hardcoded 10MB instead of actual configured limit

When the server returns a 413 (Payload Too Large) error, the client displays `I18n.t('post.errors.file_too_large', { max_size_kb: maxSizeKB })` where `maxSizeKB` is hardcoded to `10 * 1024`. If the site has configured a smaller limit (e.g., `max_image_size_kb = 2048` for 2MB), the error message will incorrectly tell the user the limit is 10MB, confusing users about why their 3MB file was rejected. The message should reflect the actual configured limit from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` or `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb` depending on the upload type.

Animation detection uses case-sensitive .GIF regex, missing .gif files

The line `method_name += "_animated" if !!opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i` uses `/\.GIF$/i` which has the `i` flag for case-insensitive matching, so this actually works correctly for `.gif`, `.GIF`, `.Gif`, etc. However, this is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase which typically uses `/\.gif$/i` (lowercase). More importantly, this regex only matches files ending in `.GIF` (case-insensitive), but animated images can also be `.webp` or other formats. The `allow_animation` option is specifically for animated GIFs, so this may be intentional, but the uppercase `GIF` in the pattern is unusual and could be a typo that happens to work due to the `i` flag.

Downsize loop runs synchronously in web request, blocking for potentially long ImageMagick operations

The downsize loop (lines 64-70) runs synchronously within the `create_upload` method, which is called either directly (synchronous API) or via `Scheduler::Defer.later` (line 19). For non-API uploads, this runs in a background job, which is acceptable. However, for synchronous API requests (line 15-17), this blocks the web worker for the duration of up to 5 ImageMagick `convert` operations plus `ImageOptim` optimization. Each operation can take several seconds for large images, potentially causing request timeouts and tying up web workers. Large image processing should be moved to a background job even for API requests, or the synchronous API path should have a separate, shorter timeout. The current implementation risks worker exhaustion under load.

Downsize uses fixed 80% reduction rather than calculating required reduction to meet size target

The downsize loop uses a fixed "80%" dimension reduction each iteration. This is inefficient: for a 50MB image with a 2MB limit, reducing dimensions by 20% each time reduces file size roughly by 36% (area scales with square of linear dimensions), so 5 iterations get to ~32% of original dimensions (~5MB file), still over the limit. The loop exits after 5 attempts regardless. A more efficient approach would calculate the target dimensions based on the ratio of current size to target size, or use ImageMagick's `-define jpeg:extent` or similar to target a specific file size directly. The current approach wastes CPU on multiple iterations that may not achieve the goal.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

unsubscribe action does not verify the user can see the topic

unsubscribe toggle logic silently does nothing for muted users and mislabels the action

The toggle in #unsubscribe is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted end`. For a user whose level is already `muted` (0), the condition is false, so the level is set to `muted` again — the link never restores notifications for muted users, it only ever mutes or downgrades. Additionally, the email copy says 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic', but for watching/tracking users the action only downgrades to regular (they still get emails), which contradicts the promise in the email and the client-side text 'You will stop receiving notifications'. After mutating the notification level, #unsubscribe calls `perform_show_response`, which serializes the entire TopicView (all posts the guardian can see) and, for HTML requests, calls `store_preloaded("topic_#{id}", ...)` and renders :show. The unsubscribe endpoint is meant to be a lightweight landing page reached from an email link; rendering the full topic leaks the topic body to anyone with the URL (subject only to normal guardian checks, which are not explicitly performed here) and does heavy work. It should render a minimal confirmation instead of the full topic payload.

check_xhr is skipped for unsubscribe, allowing non-XHR state-changing GET `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` permits the state-changing `unsubscribe` action to be triggered by a plain GET request from any context, including via CSRF-style link prefetching or cross-site /link tags (the endpoint is same-origin but a cross-site GET from a browser is still possible since no CSRF token is required for GET). Combined with the missing visibility check, this makes the notification-level mutation triggerable by simple navigation. A POST/PUT route or an explicit confirmation would be safer.

topic-unsubscribe route creates a record in the store that is never cleaned up and fetches data needlessly

The route's model hook calls `this.store.createRecord("topic", { id: params.id })`, which inserts a new (unsaved, id-only) Topic record into the Ember Data store, then immediately overwrites it via `topic.updateFromJson(json)` from `PostStream.loadTopicView`. Creating a store record for an id-only object pollutes the identity map (a later real fetch of the same topic id may return this stub), and `loadTopicView` duplicates the normal topic-loading path. The route should use `this.store.find('topic', params.id)` or the standard topic model hook instead of createRecord.

afterModel sets a nested property path that Ember cannot observe on a plain object

`topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` assumes `topic.details` is an Ember object; if `details` is a plain JS object (as serialized topic details typically are in this codebase), setting a nested path on it will not be tracked and may silently fail or throw depending on the Ember version. The intent (hide the notification reason text on the unsubscribe page) is not reliably achieved.

Triple-stache output of stopNotificiationsText injects the topic title as raw HTML The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (unescaped). The string is built from `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`. `fancyTitle` is HTML-escaped server-side (ERB::Util.html_escape in Topic#fancy_title), but I18n interpolation does not re-escape, and any locale override or future change to the title source would inject raw HTML into the page. The locale string itself contains `{{title}}`, so the title must be escaped before interpolation (e.g. via `Em.I18n` with escaped params or by escaping in the controller) rather than relying on the server-side escaping surviving the round trip.

dropdown-button renderString interpolates unescaped values into HTML (XSS) renderString builds HTML by string concatenation: `buffer.push("
  • ")` and `buffer.push("" + row.title + "")` etc. None of `id`, `row.title`, `row.description`, `row.styleClasses`, `this.get('text')`, `title`, or `longDescription` are HTML-escaped. Any caller that passes user-controlled data (e.g. topic titles, category names) into dropDownContent/text will produce an XSS vulnerability. The component should escape all interpolated values (e.g. with a Handlebars escape or _.escape) before pushing them into the buffer.

unsubscribe_url passed to emails points to a login-required page with no key, so email clients cannot use it

`send_notification_email` sets `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, which is `#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}/unsubscribe`. The TopicsController#unsubscribe action is behind `ensure_logged_in`, so a recipient opening the link from an email (typically not logged in, or in a mail client with no Discourse session) is bounced to the login page and the unsubscribe never happens. Unlike the digest's `@unsubscribe_key` (DigestUnsubscribeKey), there is no per-user token authenticating this URL. Either the route must accept an authenticated key (like email/unsubscribe/:key) or the link must be removed; as shipped the 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' link in every notification email is broken for logged-out users.

List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL

In `header_args`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is set the `List-Unsubscribe` header is set to `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>` — the generic preferences page — even though the PR adds a per-topic `unsubscribe_url` to template_args. Mail clients that expose a one-click unsubscribe (RFC 2369/8058) will therefore send users to preferences rather than actually unsubscribing from the topic, and the header does not reflect the new per-topic capability. The header should use `template_args[:unsubscribe_url]` when present (falling back to user_preferences_url), and ideally include a `mailto:` alternative per RFC 8058.

body appends unsubscribe text unconditionally when add_unsubscribe_link is set, even if body is nil

`body` does `body = @opts[:body]` then, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, executes `body << "\n"`. If `@opts[:body]` is nil (callers that rely on a template, e.g. `template: 'user_notifications.signup'`, pass no :body), this raises NoMethodError on nil. The guard should check that body is present (or initialize it to a String) before appending.

unsubscribe_link placeholder only substituted in html_part, not in the plain-text body template

The HTML email template now contains `%{unsubscribe_link}`, and `html_part` substitutes it via `html_override.gsub!("%{unsubscribe_link}", ...)`. However the plain-text path (`MessageBuilder#body`) appends `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` directly, which is fine, but any other HTML template that contains `%{unsubscribe_link}` and is rendered through a path that does not go through `html_part`'s gsub (or templates rendered before this change) will leak the literal `%{unsubscribe_link}` placeholder to recipients. The substitution should be centralized so both HTML and text bodies get the placeholder replaced consistently.

unsubscribe_link locale string promises per-topic unsubscribe that requires login

The new locale text says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).' but the target URL requires an authenticated session (see TopicsController#unsubscribe ensure_logged_in) and has no per-user token, so recipients opening it from email are redirected to login and the promised action does not occur. The copy overpromises; either fix the endpoint to work logged-out (token-based) or reword the copy.

No test verifies the per-topic unsubscribe_url appears in the email body or List-Unsubscribe header

The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the builder under test but only asserts that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains the user_preferences_url. Nothing asserts that the body contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL (via the updated `unsubscribe_link` locale string) nor that the List-Unsubscribe header uses it. The core behavior of this PR — the per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails — is untested, and the header assertion would still pass with the old preferences-only header.

No controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint

The PR adds a new `unsubscribe` action and two new routes (`t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) but includes no specs covering: the nil TopicUser case, the toggle behavior for muted vs watching users, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, the login requirement, or the response format. Given the endpoint mutates notification state and is linked from every notification email, request specs are needed before merge.

topicUnsubscribe route is registered as a top-level route instead of nested under the topic resource

`this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared outside the `this.resource('topic', ...)` block, so it does not inherit the topic resource's model/controller context. The route's model hook therefore cannot use `this.modelFor('topic')` and must re-fetch the topic itself (which it does via createRecord/loadTopicView). Nesting it under the topic resource (`this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` inside the resource) would give it the parent topic model for free and match the server route structure.
